hero.title: The bar's inventory, reconciled at closing.
hero.subtitle: Every dispatch from the cellar, every supplier delivery and every breakage lands in a ledger that is never edited. Stock is what that ledger adds up to, not a number somebody types in.
hero.note: Built for bars, casinos and restaurants that dispatch bottle by bottle. Access is by invitation.

features.title: What it solves
features.subtitle: Four things a shared spreadsheet cannot hold up.

ledger.title: A ledger that is never rewritten
ledger.body: Every movement keeps its author, its date and its reason. Voiding does not erase: it writes the reversal, and the history still adds up.

stock.title: Stock that derives itself
stock.body: Each location's stock is updated in the same transaction that confirms the movement, and every product's kardex shows the running balance line by line.

roles.title: Whoever dispatches does not adjust
roles.body: Operators register dispatches. Inbounds, transfers, adjustments and voids need a manager, and every adjustment carries a mandatory reason.

reports.title: Consumption, in numbers
reports.body: How much left, of what and over which period, aggregated in the database. Every movement downloads as a PDF carrying your operation's details.

how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: Three steps, and the third one is where the answers are.

capture.title: Capture
capture.body: Pick the location, the date and the products, in bottles or in cases. The draft saves itself: close the browser and it is still there.

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.body: Confirming applies the movement's delta to stock in a single transaction. A dispatch larger than what the location holds is refused.

read.title: Read
read.body: Stock per location, a kardex per product, consumption reports and an audit log that says who did what, when and from where.

locations.question: Does it handle several locations?
locations.answer: Yes. Every stock level and every ledger line belongs to one location, and a transfer moves units between two without changing the total on hand.

mistakes.question: What if I record something wrong?
mistakes.answer: A confirmed movement is voided with a reason and stock comes back; the movement is kept, marked as cancelled. For a count variance there is the adjustment, which also demands a reason.

cases.question: How are cases counted?
cases.answer: Each product declares how many singles a case holds and the system normalizes every quantity to base units. You capture in cases and read in units, without doing the arithmetic.

roles.question: Who gets to see what?
roles.answer: Four roles behind one declarative permission matrix that lives on the server. The interface hides what you cannot do, but what actually stops it is the API.

cta.title: Start with stock at zero
cta.body: A new business starts with nothing on hand: stock appears when somebody records the first inbound. Nothing is invented for you.

OUTBOUND.label: Dispatch
OUTBOUND.effect: Stock leaves the cellar when you confirm. Nothing moves before that.

INBOUND.label: Inbound
INBOUND.effect: What the supplier delivered. Confirming adds it to stock.

ADJUSTMENT.label: Adjustment
ADJUSTMENT.effect: Breakage, spillage or a count that did not match. Quantities go negative to take units out, positive to put them back, and the reason is part of the record.

TRANSFER.label: Transfer
TRANSFER.effect: Moves stock from one location to another. The total on hand does not change: confirming writes both sides at once.
